Provenance: Charles Reade, George Hart, Joseph Gillott, The Earl of Dunmore, John Adam, David Laurie, Richard Bennett, Frederick Smith, Empsall, Hart & Son, Ferencz Heyedüs. Literature: Hill (Alfred, Arthur & W. Henry) Violin Makers of the Guarneri Family, p. 101. Hart & Son, A Violin by Joseph Guarnerius del Gesu 1734, monograph. Hart (G.) The Violin, Famous Makers and their Imitators, pp. 255, 323. Davidson (P.) The Violin, Its construction, theoretically and practically treated, p. 224. History: The violin was brought to England by Charles Reade, author of “The Cloister and the Hearth”, novelist and violin collector. It was later sold by George Hart to Joseph Gillott. Gillott was a pen manufacturer and amassed one of the largest and finest private collections of violins ever formed. Part of the collection was dispersed at a sale at Christie's on 29th April 1872. The present instrument was included in that sale when it realised the second highest price £275, the highest price of £290 being realised by the ‘Emperor’ Stradivari of 1715. The catalogue and indeed George Hart in his book The Violin, Famous makers and their Imitators both misdate the instrument, stating it to be from 1732. The Violin was purchased by the Earl of Dunmore. On his death the instrument became part of the collection of John Adam (another Joseph Guarneri del Jesu from this collection, the ex-Adam of 1738, was sold in these rooms on 12th May 1977). The Adam Collection was purchased in 1882 by David Laurie of Glasgow, the leading international dealer of his day and was sold by him to Richard Bennett. Mr. Bennett's collection was dispersed in 1892 at which time the Gillott Guarneri passed into the hands of another collector Frederick Smith who eventually sold it to a friend Mr. Empsall, from whom Hart & Son purchased the instrument some thirty years later. They sold it to the Hungarian born violist and conductor Ferencz Hegedüs. Shortly before his death in 1944 the violin came back into the possession of Hart & Son, at which time they published their monograph on it. (See Colour Illustration)
